| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Facet` | string |  |  |  | Restrict to 'function' or 'worksWith'. Omit for both. Allowed: function, worksWith. |
| `-Counts` | switch | `$true` |  |  | Append each value's tool count, e.g. 'binaries (8)'. Default: on. Use -Counts:$false to print the terms alone. |

**Outputs:** System.String[]

**Example 1**

```powershell
Get-DFCategoryList
```

Prints both vocabularies with counts.

**Example 2**

```powershell
tcats -Facet function -Counts:$false
```

The valid -Category values under a Function heading, without counts.

**Example 3**

```powershell
tcats -Facet function -Counts:$false | Where-Object { $_ -like '  *' } | ForEach-Object Trim
```

Just the terms, one per line, for use in a script.

**See also:** [package-catalog](guide/package-catalog.md)

### Select-DFPackage

Alias: `ftrifle`

Fuzzy-browse packages with fzf. With a query: searches every catalog (like trifle) and previews each result's info card; Enter renders the full detail card. Without a query: browses all locally cached packages.

```text
Select-DFPackage [[-Query] <string[]>] [-Categories] [-Category <string>] [-WorksWith <string>] [-Source <string[]>] [-Readme] [-GitInfo] [<CommonParameters>]
```

Query mode pre-renders each result's basic info card to a temp file so the fzf preview is instant — no subprocess module loads, no network while scrolling. The selection re-enters Find-DFPackage via its qualified source:packageId, which fetches full per-catalog details.

Browse mode (no query) reads only local caches (scoop/winget indexes, cached web queries, the installed snapshot) so the list opens instantly — run Update-DFPackageCache (or any first trifle query) to populate it.

Requires fzf (or $Env:Picker). Query mode writes preview files to a per-process folder under the system temp directory and removes it when the picker closes. Network use is the same as Find-DFPackage.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Query` | string[] |  |  | remaining args | Search terms. When present, the list is live search results with a detail-card pipeline; when absent, the local-cache browser. |
| `-Categories` | switch |  |  |  | Browse the full taxonomy vocabulary (every function/works-with value, live tool counts); Enter drills into the picked facet. |
| `-Category` | string |  |  |  | Search this specific function value directly — same preview/selection flow as -Query. |
| `-WorksWith` | string |  |  |  | Search this specific works-with value directly — same preview/selection flow as -Query. Set internally when -Categories recurses into a picked works-with row; also usable directly. |
| `-Source` | string[] |  |  |  | Restrict to packages known to these catalogs: scoop, winget, choco, npm, pypi, crates, psgallery. Default: all seven. |
| `-Readme` | switch |  |  |  | After selection, also fetch and page the package readme. |
| `-GitInfo` | switch |  |  |  | After selection, include GitHub stars/release/activity on the card. |

**Outputs:** None — the selection is rendered via Find-DFPackage.

**Example 1**

```powershell
ftrifle zed
```

Search all catalogs for 'zed', preview cards while scrolling, Enter shows the full detail card.

**Example 2**

```powershell
ftrifle
```

Browse all locally known packages; Enter renders the info card.

**Example 3**

```powershell
ftrifle -Categories
```

Pick a category or works-with value from the full vocabulary; Enter drills into that facet's tools with the same preview/selection flow as a query.

**See also:** [package-catalog](guide/package-catalog.md)

### Update-DFCategoryDb

Downloads the latest published trifle category database and installs it under $XDG_DATA_HOME/dotforge/, taking precedence over the module's shipped copy on the next load.

```text
Update-DFCategoryDb [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

Purely opt-in — never runs implicitly, not part of Update-DFPackageCache, not triggered by any trifle/ftrifle call. Discovery stays fully usable offline with the shipped seed data by default. Validates the download before writing; a failed download or a failed validation leaves any existing refreshed copy untouched and warns instead of throwing.

Downloads tool-categories.json from the latest DotForge GitHub release and writes $XDG_DATA_HOME\\dotforge\\tool-categories.json (atomically, through a temp file). Delete that file to go back to the shipped copy. Supports -WhatIf and -Confirm.

**Outputs:** None. Writes one line to the host on success.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Update-DFCategoryDb
```

Fetches and installs the latest published category database.

**Example 2**

```powershell
Update-DFCategoryDb -WhatIf
```

Shows what would be written without touching disk.

**See also:** [package-catalog](guide/package-catalog.md)

### Update-DFPackageCache

Refreshes all catalog caches used by Find-DFPackage (trifle) — and does nothing else. Designed to run from Task Scheduler so interactive queries always answer from warm caches.

```text
Update-DFPackageCache [[-Source] <string[]>] [-Quiet] [<CommonParameters>]
```

Runs synchronously and sequentially (it IS the background work): rebuilds snapshot indexes (scoop bucket index, winget SQLite extraction), refreshes the unified installed-package snapshot, then re-fetches every recently seen query plus the exact name of every installed tool against each web catalog. Also re-warms every cached package-detail entry (readme/GitHub/install-hint data fetched by `trifle`'s detail card) — the files under each provider's `details/` cache directory ARE the re-warm list, keyed off the raw PackageId stored in each entry. Safe to run while an interactive session is open — all cache writes are atomic renames, so last writer wins and both stay valid.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Source` | string[] |  |  |  | Restrict the refresh to these catalogs: scoop, winget, choco, npm, pypi, crates, psgallery. Default: all seven. |
| `-Quiet` | switch |  |  |  | Suppress progress output (Task Scheduler mode); warnings still flow. |

**Outputs:** None. Writes cache files under $XDG_CACHE_HOME\\dotforge\\catalogs and makes the same network requests as Find-DFPackage, once per cached query and detail entry.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Update-DFPackageCache
```

Full refresh with progress messages.

**Example 2**

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -Command "winget source update; Import-Module DotForge; Update-DFPackageCache -Quiet"
```

The Task Scheduler action for a nightly catalog refresh. `winget source update` runs first — see NOTES for why.

**See also:** [package-catalog](guide/package-catalog.md)

### Update-DFToolIdentityGuide

Downloads the latest published trifle tool-identity guide and installs it under $XDG_DATA_HOME/dotforge/, taking precedence over the module's shipped copy on the next load.

```text
Update-DFToolIdentityGuide [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

Purely opt-in — never runs implicitly, not part of Update-DFPackageCache, not triggered by any trifle/ftrifle call. Cross-catalog identity resolution stays fully usable offline with the shipped seed guide by default (and always falls back further to the live Tools/\*.json mechanism regardless of guide state). Validates the download before writing; a failed download or a failed validation leaves any existing refreshed copy untouched and warns instead of throwing.

Downloads tool-identities.json from the latest DotForge GitHub release and writes $XDG_DATA_HOME\\dotforge\\tool-identities.json (atomically, through a temp file). Delete that file to go back to the shipped copy. Supports -WhatIf and -Confirm.

**Outputs:** None. Writes one line to the host on success.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Update-DFToolIdentityGuide
```

Fetches and installs the latest published tool-identity guide.

**Example 2**

```powershell
Update-DFToolIdentityGuide -WhatIf
```

Shows what would be written without touching disk.

**See also:** [package-catalog](guide/package-catalog.md)

## Roles

A role is a job several tools can do. For a *single* role, one installed tool wins (`$DFConfig.Defaults`, else the highest priority) and only it sets the role's variables and aliases and installs its hooks. A *category* only groups tools. Run `Get-DFRole` to see the winners on your machine.

### completion role

Adds or improves Tab completion.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [carapace](#carapace-tool), [inshellisense](#inshellisense-tool), [PSFzf](#psfzf-tool), [psreadline](#psreadline-tool) |

### diff role

Displays git diffs. The winner sets GIT_PAGER.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [delta](#delta-tool) |
| Only the winner sets | `GIT_PAGER` |

### directory-jump role

Changes to a folder you pick from Alt+C. Only the winner binds the key; a binding you made yourself is kept.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [broot](#broot-tool), [fzf](#fzf-tool), [skim](#skim-tool) |

### editor role

Edits text files. The winner sets EDITOR and VISUAL.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [micro](#micro-tool) |
| Only the winner sets | `EDITOR`, `VISUAL` |

### elevator role

Runs a command with administrator rights. Install-DFTool runs a manager that needs admin (choco) through it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [gsudo](#gsudo-tool) |

### file-search role

Finds files by name.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [fd](#fd-tool) |

### fuzzy-finder role

Filters a list interactively as you type.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [fzf](#fzf-tool), [gum](#gum-tool), [peco](#peco-tool), [skim](#skim-tool), [television](#television-tool) |

### grep role

Searches file contents.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [ripgrep](#ripgrep-tool) |

### history-search role

Searches command history from Ctrl+R. Only the winner binds the key; a binding you made yourself is kept.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [fzf](#fzf-tool), [PSFzf](#psfzf-tool), [skim](#skim-tool), [television](#television-tool) |

### js-package-manager role

Installs packages from the npm registry. Install-DFTool uses the Defaults choice, else the highest priority.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [bun](#bun-tool), [npm](#npm-tool), [pnpm](#pnpm-tool) |

### js-runtime role

Provides a JavaScript runtime on PATH (node, bun). Tools that need one declare requires: ["role:js-runtime"].

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [bun](#bun-tool), [node](#node-tool) |

### listing role

Lists directory contents. The winner defines ls, ll, la, tree and ff.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [eza](#eza-tool), [lsd](#lsd-tool) |
| Only the winner sets | `ls`, `ll`, `la`, `tree`, `ff` |

### markdown-viewer role

Renders Markdown in the terminal.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [glow](#glow-tool), [mdcat](#mdcat-tool), [mdv](#mdv-tool) |

### navigation role

Jumps to frequently used directories. Hooks the prompt to track directory changes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single, exclusive |
| Members | [zoxide](#zoxide-tool) |

### package-manager role

Installs tools. Install-DFTool tries the winner first, then the others by priority.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [choco](#choco-tool), [scoop](#scoop-tool), [winget](#winget-tool) |

### pager role

Pages long output. The winner sets PAGER and BAT_PAGER, which DotForge's own pager also reads; with no pager, more.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [less](#less-tool), [moor](#moor-tool), [ov](#ov-tool) |
| Only the winner sets | `PAGER`, `BAT_PAGER` |
| With no winner | `PAGER` = `more`, `BAT_PAGER` = `more` |

### path-insert role

Inserts picked paths at the cursor from Ctrl+T. Only the winner binds the key; a binding you made yourself is kept.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [fzf](#fzf-tool), [PSFzf](#psfzf-tool), [skim](#skim-tool), [television](#television-tool) |

### picker role

Fuzzy-picks from a list. The winner sets Picker, which every DotForge picker runs.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [fzf](#fzf-tool), [skim](#skim-tool) |
| Only the winner sets | `Picker` |
| Requires | Accepts fzf's command-line options and reads candidates on stdin. |

### powershell-package-manager role

Installs modules from the PowerShell Gallery.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [psresource](#psresource-tool) |

### project-env role

Loads per-directory environment variables. Two active hooks would fight over the same variables.

| | |
| --- | --- |

| Members | [direnv](#direnv-tool), [mise](#mise-tool), [ps-dotenv](#ps-dotenv-tool) |

### prompt role

Draws the shell prompt. Only one prompt engine may own the prompt function.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single, exclusive |
| Members | [oh-my-posh](#oh-my-posh-tool), [starship](#starship-tool) |

### python-package-manager role

Installs packages from PyPI. Install-DFTool uses the Defaults choice, else the highest priority (uv, pipx, pip).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [pip](#pip-tool), [pipx](#pipx-tool), [uv](#uv-tool) |

### python-runtime role

Provides a Python runtime on PATH. Tools that need one declare requires: ["role:python-runtime"].

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [python](#python-tool) |

### rust-package-manager role

Installs crates from crates.io.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [cargo](#cargo-tool) |

### system-info role

Shows system information.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [fastfetch](#fastfetch-tool) |

### tab-completion role

Owns the Tab key. The winner binds Tab; the others still register their completers.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | single |
| Members | [carapace](#carapace-tool), [inshellisense](#inshellisense-tool), [PSFzf](#psfzf-tool) |

### url-fetch role

Downloads files and calls HTTP APIs.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [curl](#curl-tool), [wget](#wget-tool) |

### version-manager role

Installs and switches language runtime versions.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | category |
| Members | [fnm](#fnm-tool), [mise](#mise-tool), [pymanager](#pymanager-tool), [rustup](#rustup-tool), [uv](#uv-tool) |

## Tool records

What `Register-DFTool` does for each tool, read from its `Tools/<name>.json` record. A tool is configured only when it is detected: its executable is on `PATH`, or for a module, the module is installed. For the record format, see [Writing a tool record](guide/writing-a-tool.md).

## Tool companion functions

These are defined when their tool is registered (`Register-DFTool`), not when the module is imported. Each needs its tool installed.

### bitwarden companion

#### Select-BwItem

Alias: `fbw`

Fuzzy-picks a Bitwarden vault item and copies its password, clearing the clipboard after 30 seconds.

Checks bw status first: a vault that is logged out or locked gets the command to fix it, and nothing is listed. Otherwise lists the vault's items (name and username; no secrets), and Enter copies the chosen item's password to the clipboard. After 30 seconds DotForge clears the clipboard, but only if it still holds that password, so something you copied since is left alone. The clearing runs in a separate hidden process (given only a hash of the password), so it still happens if you close the shell first. An item with no password (a secure note, a card) gets a warning.

Windows clipboard history (Win+V) and clipboard sync may keep their own copy of the password; turn them off if that matters to you.

Defined by DotForge's bitwarden companion. Requires fzf (or $Env:Picker) and an unlocked vault (BW_SESSION set, e.g. $Env:BW_SESSION = bw unlock --raw).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Type` | string | `'all'` |  |  | List only this kind of item: login, note, card, identity, or all (default). Allowed: login, note, card, identity, all. |

**Outputs:** None. The password goes to the clipboard only.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fbw -Type login
```

Picks a login and copies its password for 30 seconds.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### broot companion

#### br

Runs broot, and moves the shell to the folder you leave it in.

Opens broot in the current folder with your arguments. Leave it with a cd (alt+enter, or :cd) and the shell changes to that folder, through zoxide's cd when zoxide is your navigation tool; quit without one and nothing changes. broot's skin follows BrootTheme (Set-DFToolTheme broot &lt;flavor&gt; switches it).

Every argument goes to broot as it is (a folder to open, -f, -d, -p, ...): br is a simple function, so PowerShell doesn't take -d for -Debug. Defined by DotForge's broot companion. It replaces broot's own br, which DotForge's setup tells broot not to install.

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
br
```

Browses the current folder; alt+enter on a folder moves the shell there.

**Example 2**

```powershell
br -f -d $HOME\projects
```

Browses only the folders under your projects folder, with dates.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### choco companion

#### Assert-DFChoco

Returns $true when choco is on PATH; otherwise warns and returns $false.

Guard used by the choco pickers (cins, crm, cup). Defined by DotForge's choco companion.

**Outputs:** System.Boolean.

**Example 1**

```powershell
if (Assert-DFChoco) { choco list }
```

Runs choco only when it is installed.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Invoke-ChocoUpdate

Alias: `cup`

Fuzzy-picks outdated Chocolatey packages and upgrades them.

Lists packages with a newer version (choco outdated: installed -&gt; available) in fzf with a choco info preview.

```text
Keys:
  Tab     mark a package (repeat for several)
  Enter   upgrade the marked packages, or the highlighted one
  Alt-A   run choco upgrade all -y
```

Defined by DotForge's choco companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker). Installing, uninstalling and upgrading need an elevated shell: they run through gsudo when DotForge's sudo alias points at it, which shows a UAC prompt; otherwise choco itself fails without admin rights.

**Outputs:** None. choco writes its own progress.

**Example 1**

```powershell
cup
```

Mark packages with Tab, then press Enter to upgrade them.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Invoke-DFChocoElevated

Runs choco with the given arguments, elevated through gsudo when available.

When DotForge's sudo alias points at gsudo, runs sudo choco &lt;args&gt;, which shows a UAC prompt; otherwise runs choco &lt;args&gt; directly, and choco fails without admin rights for commands that need them. Defined by DotForge's choco companion.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-ChocoArgs` | string[] |  |  | remaining args | Arguments passed to choco unchanged. |

**Outputs:** Whatever choco writes.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFChocoElevated upgrade ripgrep -y
```

Upgrades ripgrep from an unelevated shell.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Remove-ChocoPackage

Alias: `crm`

Fuzzy-picks an installed Chocolatey package and uninstalls it.

Lists installed packages (choco list) in fzf with a choco info preview.

```text
Keys:
  Enter   uninstall the selection
  Alt-X   uninstall the highlighted package without closing the picker
  Alt-C   return the command 'choco uninstall <id> -y' instead
```

Defined by DotForge's choco companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker). Installing, uninstalling and upgrading need an elevated shell: they run through gsudo when DotForge's sudo alias points at it, which shows a UAC prompt; otherwise choco itself fails without admin rights.

**Outputs:** System.String (the uninstall command) on Alt-C; otherwise none.

**Example 1**

```powershell
crm
```

Pick an installed package and press Enter to uninstall it.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-ChocoPackage

Alias: `cins`

Searches the Chocolatey community feed, fuzzy-picks a package, and returns or runs its install command.

Runs choco search for -Query and lists the results in fzf with a choco info preview, shown after the cursor rests on an item for about a second.

```text
Keys:
  Enter   return the command 'choco install <id> -y' (nothing is
          installed; run it in an elevated shell)
  Alt-R   close the picker and install the selection now
  Alt-I   install the highlighted package without closing the picker
```

Bound to Ctrl+G, C when PSReadLine is loaded: type a search term, press the chord, pick a package, and the install command replaces the line.

Defined by DotForge's choco companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker). Installing, uninstalling and upgrading need an elevated shell: they run through gsudo when DotForge's sudo alias points at it, which shows a UAC prompt; otherwise choco itself fails without admin rights.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Query` | string | `''` |  |  | Search terms passed to choco search. When omitted, you are prompted. |

**Outputs:** System.String (the install command) on Enter; otherwise none.

**Example 1**

```powershell
cins ripgrep
```

Pick ripgrep and press Enter to get: choco install ripgrep -y

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### fnm companion

#### Set-LocationWithFnm

Changes directory (through zoxide when it is registered) and switches Node versions for the new directory.

DotForge's replacement for the function fnm env --use-on-cd defines. The cd alias points here. It forwards all arguments to whatever owned cd before fnm registered (zoxide's smart cd, or Set-Location), then runs fnm's Set-FnmOnLoad, which switches to the Node version named by a .node-version or .nvmrc file in the new directory.

Defined by DotForge's fnm companion. You normally call it as cd.

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
cd ~/projects/web-app
```

Changes directory, then fnm activates the Node version that the project's .nvmrc names.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### fzf companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyFzfTheme

Applies an fzf color theme to this session by appending a --color option to FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS.

Resolves -Name to a theme file: an absolute path is used as is, otherwise $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\fzf\\themes\\&lt;Name&gt;.json, then DotForge's bundled Tools\\fzf\\&lt;Name&gt;.json. The file's "colors" object of fzf color names and values becomes one --color=name:value,... option appended to $Env:FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS, so it applies to every later fzf call in the session. Each call appends another --color option; fzf applies them in order, so the last theme applied wins.

Every entry is checked against fzf's --color grammar (hex like #1e1e2e, -1, 0-255, default, or a color name, each optionally followed by :bold, :underline and similar), and invalid entries are skipped with a warning. An unknown theme name warns and changes nothing.

Defined by DotForge's fzf companion, which calls it at startup with $DFConfig.FzfTheme, then $DFConfig.Theme, then catppuccin-mocha.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | A theme name (e.g. catppuccin-mocha) or the full path to a theme JSON file. |
| `-Implicit` | switch |  |  |  | Used by the companion at startup when the theme came from $DFConfig.Theme or the default: an FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS you set outside DotForge is then kept as is. Without it (calling the function yourself, or an explicit FzfTheme), the colors are appended to it. |

**Outputs:** None. Changes $Env:FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS for the current session.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyFzfTheme -Name catppuccin-mocha
```

Applies the bundled Catppuccin Mocha colors to fzf for this session.

**Example 2**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyFzfTheme -Name "$HOME\dotfiles\fzf-gruvbox.json"
```

Applies a theme file you wrote, e.g. { "colors": { "bg": "#282828", "fg": "#ebdbb2" } }.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### glow companion

Alias: `fgl`

**Outputs:** None.

```powershell
fgl docs
```

Picks a Markdown file under docs and reads it in glow.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### gsudo companion

#### please

Re-runs the previous command elevated, through gsudo.

Takes the last entry in this session's history (Get-History) and runs it again through gsudo, which shows a UAC prompt. Pipes, semicolons and other compound syntax are preserved. Warns and does nothing when there is no history yet.

The command runs in a new elevated PowerShell process, so variables and functions from the current session are not available to it.

Defined by DotForge's gsudo companion, which also aliases sudo to gsudo and, when Windows' built-in sudo.exe would otherwise win, moves gsudo's directory to the front of PATH.

**Outputs:** Whatever the elevated command writes.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Remove-Item C:\Windows\Temp\old.log
please
```

The first command fails with access denied; please runs it again elevated.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### gum companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyGumTheme

Applies a gum color theme to this session through gum's GUM_\* color variables.

Resolves -Name to a theme file: an absolute path is used as is, otherwise $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\gum\\themes\\&lt;Name&gt;.json, then DotForge's bundled Tools\\gum\\&lt;Name&gt;.json. Each entry of the file's "env" object (a GUM_\* variable and a #rrggbb color) is set for this session; a variable you set outside DotForge is kept unless you call this yourself. Entries that aren't GUM_\* variables with a hex color are skipped with a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | A theme name (e.g. catppuccin-mocha) or the full path to a theme JSON file. |
| `-Implicit` | switch |  |  |  | Used by the companion at startup when the theme came from Theme or the default: a GUM_\* variable you set outside DotForge is then kept as is. |

**Outputs:** None. Changes GUM_\* environment variables for the current session.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyGumTheme -Name catppuccin-frappe
```

Switches gum to the bundled Catppuccin Frappé colors for this session.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### inshellisense companion

#### Start-DFInshellisense

Starts an inshellisense session in this shell unless one is already running.

Checks is -c, which succeeds inside an existing inshellisense session, and returns without doing anything in that case. Otherwise it runs the script printed by is init pwsh, which starts inshellisense's IDE-style autocomplete in the current shell.

DotForge calls this when inshellisense wins the tab-completion role. Defined by DotForge's inshellisense companion; requires the is command.

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Start-DFInshellisense
```

Starts inshellisense in the current shell.

**See also:** [completion](guide/completion.md)

### jq companion

#### Select-JsonPath

Alias: `fjq`

A live jq playground: type a filter in fzf, watch its output, and press Enter to run it.

Opens fzf on a JSON file with the query box as the jq filter (starting at '.'). The preview shows jq's output for the filter as you type it; Enter runs the filter on the file and writes jq's output to the pipeline. Esc runs nothing.

Without -Path, first picks a \*.json file below the current folder (with fd when it is installed, else Get-ChildItem).

A filter that contains double quotes may not preview correctly, but Enter passes it to jq unchanged.

Defined by DotForge's jq companion. Requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Path` | string |  |  |  | The JSON file. When omitted, you pick one. |

**Outputs:** System.String. jq's output for the chosen filter.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fjq package.json
```

Opens the playground on package.json; type .dependencies and press Enter to print them.

**Example 2**

```powershell
$names = fjq data.json
```

Captures the output of the filter you settle on.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### npm companion

#### Select-NpmScript

Alias: `fns`

Fuzzy-picks a script from the nearest package.json and runs it with the project's package manager.

Finds package.json in the current folder or the nearest parent, lists its scripts with each one's command line in the preview, and runs the chosen script from the package's folder. The manager is the project's own, judged by the lockfile next to package.json: pnpm for pnpm-lock.yaml, bun for bun.lock or bun.lockb, yarn for yarn.lock, else npm.

Defined by DotForge's npm companion. Requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** The script's output.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fns
```

Picks a script such as build or test and runs it.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### oh-my-posh companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyOhMyPoshTheme

Switches the oh-my-posh prompt to a theme for this session.

Re-initializes oh-my-posh with &lt;Name&gt;.omp.json from POSH_THEMES_PATH, else DotForge's bundled catppuccin themes. It is an explicit choice, so it replaces your own config for the rest of the session. Like fpot, re-initializing replaces the prompt function, so zoxide's directory tracking stops until the next session (a known limitation).

Defined by DotForge's oh-my-posh companion when oh-my-posh is your prompt; Set-DFToolTheme oh-my-posh &lt;flavor&gt; calls it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | The oh-my-posh theme name, e.g. catppuccin_latte. |

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Set-DFToolTheme oh-my-posh catppuccin-latte
```

Switches the prompt to catppuccin latte.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-PoshTheme

Alias: `fpot`

Fuzzy-picks an oh-my-posh theme with a live prompt preview and applies it to this session.

Lists the \*.omp.json themes in $Env:POSH_THEMES_PATH in fzf, previewing each one's rendered prompt. DotForge sets POSH_THEMES_PATH to $XDG_DATA_HOME\\oh-my-posh\\themes, so copy the themes you want to browse there. Enter re-initializes oh-my-posh with that theme for the current session only. To keep it, point $Env:POSH_THEME at the theme file, or copy it to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\oh-my-posh\\, before DotForge loads. Warns and does nothing when POSH_THEMES_PATH is missing.

Re-initializing replaces the prompt function, so zoxide's directory tracking stops until the next session (a known limitation).

Defined by DotForge's oh-my-posh companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. Writes a confirmation line to the host.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fpot
```

Opens the theme picker; Enter applies the highlighted theme.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### posh-git companion

#### Select-GitBranch

Alias: `fco`

Fuzzy-picks a git branch, local or remote, and checks it out.

Lists every branch from git branch --all in fzf, with the branch's recent commits (git log --oneline) in the preview pane. Enter runs git checkout on the selection. A remote branch is checked out by its short name (remotes/origin/feature becomes feature), which lets git create a local tracking branch. Esc does nothing.

Run it inside a git work tree. Defined by DotForge's posh-git companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. git checkout writes its own messages.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fco
```

Opens the branch picker; Enter switches to the highlighted branch.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-GitFile

Alias: `fga`

Fuzzy-picks changed files and stages them with git add.

Lists git status --short in fzf, previewing each file's unstaged diff. Mark several files with Tab, then press Enter to git add each one; the new git status --short is printed afterwards. For a rename, the new path is staged. Esc stages nothing.

Run it inside a git work tree. Defined by DotForge's posh-git companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** System.String. The git status --short lines after staging.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fga
```

Opens the changed-files picker; Tab marks files, Enter stages them.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-GitLog

Alias: `flog`

Fuzzy-browses the commit log and shows the selected commit.

Lists git log --oneline for the current branch in fzf, previewing each commit's full diff (git show). Enter prints the selected commit with git show. Esc does nothing. Read-only.

Run it inside a git work tree. Defined by DotForge's posh-git companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** System.String. The git show output for the selected commit.

**Example 1**

```powershell
flog
```

Opens the log picker; Enter shows the highlighted commit.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-GitStash

Alias: `fstash`

Fuzzy-picks a stash entry and applies it.

Lists git stash list in fzf, previewing each entry's patch. Enter runs git stash apply on the selection, so the entry stays in the stash list (it is applied, not popped). Esc does nothing.

Run it inside a git work tree. Defined by DotForge's posh-git companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. git stash apply writes its own messages.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fstash
```

Opens the stash picker; Enter applies the highlighted stash.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### procs companion

#### Select-Process

Alias: `fkill`

Fuzzy-picks a running process from procs' colored table and stops it.

Lists processes with procs --color=always in fzf. Enter runs Stop-Process -Confirm on the selected PID, so PowerShell asks before anything is stopped. Esc does nothing. Stopping another user's or an elevated process needs an elevated shell.

Defined by DotForge's procs companion; requires procs and fzf (or $Env:Picker). For a picker that returns process objects instead of stopping them, use Select-DFProcess (fps).

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fkill
```

Opens the process picker; Enter asks to stop the highlighted process.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### psreadline companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyPSReadLineTheme

Applies a PSReadLine syntax-color theme to this session.

Resolves -Name to a theme file: an absolute path is used as is, otherwise $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\psreadline\\themes\\&lt;Name&gt;.json, then DotForge's bundled Tools\\psreadline\\&lt;Name&gt;.json. The file holds a "colors" object mapping PSReadLine color names (Command, Parameter, String, Comment, …; see Set-PSReadLineOption -Colors) to #RRGGBB hex values, which are converted to 24-bit ANSI colors and applied with Set-PSReadLineOption -Colors. Invalid colors are skipped with a warning; an unknown theme warns and changes nothing.

Defined by DotForge's psreadline companion, which calls it at startup with $DFConfig.PSReadLineTheme, then $DFConfig.Theme, then catppuccin-mocha.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | A theme name (e.g. catppuccin-mocha) or the full path to a theme JSON file. |

**Outputs:** None. Changes PSReadLine colors for the current session.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyPSReadLineTheme -Name catppuccin-mocha
```

Applies the bundled Catppuccin Mocha colors to the command line.

**Example 2**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyPSReadLineTheme -Name "$HOME\dotfiles\prl-theme.json"
```

Applies a theme file you wrote, e.g. { "colors": { "Command": "#89b4fa", "String": "#a6e3a1" } }.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-PSReadLineTheme

Alias: `fprl`

Fuzzy-picks a PSReadLine color theme and applies it to this session.

Lists your themes in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\psreadline\\themes followed by DotForge's bundled ones (a user theme hides a bundled theme of the same name) in fzf. Enter applies the selection with Invoke-DFApplyPSReadLineTheme for the current session only, and prints how to keep it: set $DFConfig['PSReadLineTheme'] in your profile.

Defined by DotForge's psreadline companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. Writes a confirmation line to the host.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fprl
```

Opens the theme picker; Enter applies the highlighted theme.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### ripgrep companion

#### Select-RipgrepResult

Alias: `frg`

Searches files with ripgrep, fuzzy-picks a match, and opens its file in $Env:EDITOR.

Runs rg --line-number over -Path and lists every matching line in fzf, previewing the file with the match highlighted (the preview uses bat). Enter opens the selected file in $Env:EDITOR. Only the file is passed to the editor, not the line number. Esc does nothing.

Defined by DotForge's ripgrep companion; requires rg, fzf (or $Env:Picker) and, for the preview, bat. $Env:EDITOR must be set to a single command name or path.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Pattern` | string | `''` |  |  | The ripgrep regular expression to search for. When omitted, you are prompted for it. |
| `-Path` | string | `'.'` |  |  | File or directory to search. Default: the current directory. |

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
frg 'TODO'
```

Lists every TODO under the current directory; Enter opens the file.

**Example 2**

```powershell
frg 'function\s+Get-' -Path ./Public
```

Searches only the Public folder with a regular expression.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### scoop companion

#### Assert-DFScoopModule

Returns $true when the Scoop PowerShell module is available; otherwise warns and returns $false.

Guard used by the scoop pickers (sins, srm, sup). The warning includes the command that installs the module. Defined by DotForge's scoop companion.

**Outputs:** System.Boolean.

**Example 1**

```powershell
if (Assert-DFScoopModule) { Get-ScoopApp }
```

Runs a Scoop module cmdlet only when the module is present.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Invoke-ScoopUpdate

Alias: `sup`

Fuzzy-picks installed scoop apps and updates them.

Lists every installed app (the Scoop module cannot list only outdated ones) in fzf with a scoop info preview. Updating an app that is already current does nothing.

```text
Keys:
  Tab     mark an app (repeat for several)
  Enter   update the marked apps, or the highlighted one
  Alt-A   run scoop update '*' (every app)
```

Defined by DotForge's scoop companion. Requires the Scoop PowerShell module (Install-Module Scoop -Scope CurrentUser; warns and does nothing without it) and fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. scoop writes its own progress.

**Example 1**

```powershell
sup
```

Mark apps with Tab, then press Enter to update them.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Remove-ScoopPackage

Alias: `srm`

Fuzzy-picks an installed scoop app and uninstalls it.

Lists installed apps (Get-ScoopApp) in fzf with a scoop info preview.

```text
Keys:
  Enter   uninstall the selection (Uninstall-ScoopApp)
  Alt-X   uninstall the highlighted app without closing the picker
  Alt-C   return the command 'scoop uninstall <name>' instead
```

Defined by DotForge's scoop companion. Requires the Scoop PowerShell module (Install-Module Scoop -Scope CurrentUser; warns and does nothing without it) and fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** System.String (the uninstall command) on Alt-C; otherwise none.

**Example 1**

```powershell
srm
```

Pick an installed app and press Enter to uninstall it.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-ScoopPackage

Alias: `sins`

Searches scoop buckets, fuzzy-picks an app, and returns or runs its install command.

Searches with scoop-search when it is installed (fast, and matches binary names as well as app names), otherwise with the Scoop module's Find-ScoopApp, and lists the results in fzf with a scoop info preview. Only buckets you have added are searched.

```text
Keys:
  Enter   return the command 'scoop install <name>' (nothing is installed)
  Alt-R   close the picker and install the selection now
  Alt-I   install the highlighted app without closing the picker
```

Bound to Ctrl+G, S when PSReadLine is loaded: type a search term, press the chord, pick an app, and the install command replaces the line.

Defined by DotForge's scoop companion. Requires the Scoop PowerShell module (Install-Module Scoop -Scope CurrentUser; warns and does nothing without it) and fzf (or $Env:Picker).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Query` | string | `''` |  |  | Search terms. When omitted, you are prompted. |

**Outputs:** System.String (the install command) on Enter; otherwise none.

**Example 1**

```powershell
sins ripgrep
```

Pick ripgrep and press Enter to get: scoop install ripgrep

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### skim companion

#### Invoke-DFApplySkimTheme

Applies a skim color theme to this session by appending a --color option to SKIM_DEFAULT_OPTIONS.

Resolves -Name to a theme file: an absolute path is used as is, otherwise $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\\skim\\themes\\&lt;Name&gt;.json, then DotForge's bundled Tools\\skim\\&lt;Name&gt;.json. The file's "colors" object of skim color elements (fg, bg, matched, current, current_bg, ...) becomes one --color=name:value,... option appended to $Env:SKIM_DEFAULT_OPTIONS. skim merges repeated --color options in order, so the last theme applied wins. Invalid entries are skipped with a warning; an unknown theme name warns and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | A theme name (e.g. catppuccin-mocha) or the full path to a theme JSON file. |
| `-Implicit` | switch |  |  |  | Used by the companion at startup when the theme came from Theme or the default: a SKIM_DEFAULT_OPTIONS you set outside DotForge is then kept as is. Without it, the colors are appended to it. |

**Outputs:** None. Changes $Env:SKIM_DEFAULT_OPTIONS for the current session.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplySkimTheme -Name catppuccin-latte
```

Switches skim to the bundled Catppuccin Latte colors for this session.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### starship companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyStarshipTheme

Applies a catppuccin palette to starship for this session without editing your starship.toml.

When your starship.toml sets a top-level palette other than -Name, DotForge writes a copy of it to $XDG_CACHE_HOME\\dotforge\\starship with only that palette line changed (adding the palette's table when your file lacks it) and points STARSHIP_CONFIG at the copy. When the palette already matches, or your file sets none, STARSHIP_CONFIG stays on your file, so your edits show at once.

Defined by DotForge's starship companion. It runs at startup with StarshipTheme, then Theme; Set-DFToolTheme starship &lt;flavor&gt; calls it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | The starship palette name, e.g. catppuccin_latte. |
| `-Implicit` | switch |  |  |  | The theme came from the default, not a choice: a STARSHIP_CONFIG you set yourself is kept. |

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Set-DFToolTheme starship catppuccin-latte
```

Switches the prompt to latte colors from the next prompt on.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### uv companion

#### Select-UvVenv

Alias: `fvenv`

Fuzzy-picks a Python virtual environment below a folder and activates it.

Finds pyvenv.cfg files up to 4 levels below -Path (any venv: uv, python -m venv, virtualenv), previews each one (its Python version and how it was made), and runs the chosen venv's Activate.ps1, which sets VIRTUAL_ENV and PATH and defines deactivate.

Defined by DotForge's uv companion. Requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Path` | string | `'.'` |  |  | The folder to search. Default: the current folder, so the venv of the project you are in shows at once; pass ~ to search your whole home folder. |

**Outputs:** None.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fvenv
```

Picks a venv in the current project and activates it.

**Example 2**

```powershell
fvenv ~
```

Searches every venv under your home folder.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

### vivid companion

#### Invoke-DFApplyLSColorsTheme

Resolves and applies an LS_COLORS value for the named vivid theme.

Sets $Env:LS_COLORS for the current session from vivid generate &lt;Name&gt;. The generated value is cached in $XDG_CACHE_HOME\\dotforge\\ls-colors.txt, keyed by theme name, so later sessions with the same theme skip running vivid. A theme vivid doesn't know warns and changes nothing.

Defined by DotForge's vivid companion, which calls it at startup with $DFConfig.VividTheme, then $DFConfig.Theme, then catppuccin-mocha.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Pipeline | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | string |  | yes |  | A vivid theme name; list them with vivid themes. |
| `-Force` | switch |  |  |  | Bypass the cache and regenerate even when the theme name matches what's cached — use after a vivid upgrade that may have shifted a theme's palette. |
| `-Implicit` | switch |  |  |  | Used by the companion at startup when the theme came from $DFConfig.Theme or the default: an LS_COLORS you set outside DotForge is then kept. |

**Outputs:** None. Sets $Env:LS_COLORS and may write the cache files.

**Example 1**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyLSColorsTheme -Name nord
```

Switches directory-listing colors to vivid's nord theme for this session.

**Example 2**

```powershell
Invoke-DFApplyLSColorsTheme -Name catppuccin-mocha -Force
```

Regenerates the cached value, e.g. after upgrading vivid.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)

#### Select-LSColorsTheme

Alias: `fls`

Fuzzy-picks a vivid LS_COLORS theme with a live preview and applies it to this session.

Lists vivid themes in fzf, previewing each with vivid preview. Enter applies the selection through Invoke-DFApplyLSColorsTheme for the current session only, and prints how to keep it: set $DFConfig['VividTheme'] in your profile. Esc changes nothing.

Defined by DotForge's vivid companion; requires fzf (or $Env:Picker).

**Outputs:** None. Writes a confirmation line to the host.

**Example 1**

```powershell
fls
```

Opens the theme picker; Enter applies the highlighted theme.

**See also:** [tools](guide/tools.md)
